business_scope.primary_industry_name: Fractional CFO Advisory and Multicurrency Ledger Bookkeeping

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law No. 23 of 2015 (Panama AML/CFT Law, as amended by Law No. 70 of 2019); Executive Decree No. 1 of 2021 implementing the Registro de Beneficiarios Finales (UBO register); Law No. 41 of 2000 establishing the Financial Analysis Unit (UAF) and the preventive AML/CFT regime; Public Registry and UAF implementing resolutions governing resident agents, customer due diligence and ultimate beneficial owner disclosure.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of the beneficial shareholder's passport identity page
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public or competent authority in the shareholder's country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified proof of residential address of each ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility provider, bank reference, or municipal/police registration authority in country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Police/criminal record certificate or equivalent good-conduct certificate of the beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National police or judicial authority in the country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Banker's or professional reference letter together with source-of-wealth/source-of-funds declaration
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Banks, licensed professionals, or notary public in the country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of attorney appointing the Panamanian resident agent for incorporation and statutory representation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in country of origin or Panamanian notary if executed in Panama

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good standing and board resolution when a corporate shareholder is a UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate registry and corporate secretary of the jurisdiction of incorporation

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-incorporation screening by the Panamanian resident agent: (i) customer due diligence and know-your-customer (KYC) before formation; (ii) enhanced due diligence for politically exposed persons (PEPs) as defined under Law 23 of 2015 and UAF regulations; (iii) screening against the U.S. OFAC SDN list, UN Security Council Consolidated List, EU consolidated financial sanctions list, and domestic Panamanian PEP and adverse-media databases; (iv) verification of source of wealth and source of funds; (v) risk-rating of the intended virtual CFO activity as low risk; and (vi) retention of all due diligence records for at least five years.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Público de Panamá (Public Registry of Panama), including the 'Reserva de Nombre' / name-search and 'visto bueno' modules and in-person corporate services window.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must be written in Latin characters. Spanish is the official language, but a foreign-language name may be registered if presented with a Spanish transliteration or translation. The name must be distinct from any existing registered entity, must not be deceptive as to the entity's activity, nationality or legal form, and must be followed by the mandatory legal-form suffix 'S.A.' for Sociedad Anónima.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Name reservations issued by the Public Registry of Panama are valid for 30 calendar days; no general statutory extension right exists, but the resident agent may file a fresh reservation if the window expires. Upon rejection, the resident agent may submit, within five business days, a written 'recurso de reconsideración' to the General Directorate of the Public Registry under Panama's Administrative Procedure Law No. 38 of 2000. If reconsideration is denied, an 'apelación' may be filed with the hierarchical administrative superior, with final judicial recourse to the Third Administrative Chamber of the Supreme Court of Justice. Each rejected application requires a new fee and a refreshed proposed name or evidence of approval for any restricted token.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Generally acceptable for a low-risk cross-border virtual CFO service vehicle. Panamanian law requires a registered agent and a physical statutory registered office for service of process, but does not require the central management or daily operations to be physically conducted there. If the entity invoices Panamanian-source clients or establishes a physical or employee presence in Panama, a national Aviso de Operación, municipal business license, tax registration, and possible physical premises will become mandatory.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low for the proposed non-licensed, non-financial offshore service company; estimated annual risk of unannounced inspection is below 5%. The risk rises to approximately 15-25% per year if the company obtains a local Aviso de Operación, maintains a Panamanian bank account, or offers regulated public accounting services within Panama without the appropriate professional license.

Notarization of articles of incorporation and preliminary powers

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official registration tariff for Sociedad Anónima based on authorized capital schedule

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark; mandatory under Panamanian corporate law

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office / statutory seat service, first year
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark; statutory address for service of process

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory per-document fee under Hague Apostille Convention or Panamanian consular tariff

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Variable statutory fee, included as pre-incorporation contingency

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley General de Sociedades (General Corporation Law): Ley No. 32 of 26 February 1927, as amended, in particular Articles 1-14 (constitution), 25-31 (directors and meetings), 35 (officers), 48 (executive powers) and 63-65 (registered agent); implemented with Executive Decree No. 153 of 2013 (private-document and electronic incorporation) and Ley No. 5 of 2008 (registered agent requirements).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Público de Panamá (Public Registry of Panama) - Dirección General; Sección Mercantil (Mercantile Section); Vía José de Fábrega, Panama City, Republic of Panama.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Pacto Social y Estatutos (Articles of Incorporation and By-laws), executed as a notarial Escritura Pública before a Notary of the Circuit, or, where a sole shareholder elects, as a private instrument under Executive Decree No. 153 of 2013; in either case the instrument must be inscribed in the Sección Mercantil of the Public Registry.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital and no escrow or capital deposit rule. Authorized capital is freely fixed in the charter (market standard: USD 10,000 represented by 100 registered shares of USD 100.00 par value each); at least one share must be subscribed at incorporation and may remain partly paid.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTION NO. 1. At a duly convened meeting of the Board of Directors of [CORPORATION], S.A., held at the registered office on [DATE], the Directors unanimously resolve: (1) the subscription of one hundred (100) ordinary shares of USD 100.00 par value each, subscribed by the founding shareholder under the Articles of Incorporation, is accepted and recorded in the Share Register; (2) the registered office is established at [ADDRESS], Corregimiento de Bella Vista, Panama City, Panama; (3) [NAME] is appointed President, [NAME] Secretary and [NAME] Treasurer, each holding the powers granted by Law No. 32 of 1927; and (4) the President and Secretary are jointly authorized to open bank accounts and execute tax and municipal filings required by this resolution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Name Availability Search and Certificate (Certificado de Búsqueda)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá - Online name-search module and Certificaciones Section
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a written or online application for a certified name-search certificate ('Certificado de Búsqueda') verifying that the proposed corporate name is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing inscription. Indicate two alternative names on the application. The certificate evidences availability of the name for the subsequent incorporation filing; it does not reserve the name for the applicant.
required_dossiers: Completed search application form
First and second proposed corporate names
Applicant passport or cédula copy
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name conflicts with a prior inscription, obtain a fresh search certificate citing alternative names; the certificate is not a definitive administrative act, so no formal appeal is required.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution and Notarization of the Incorporation Instrument
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary of the Circuit of Panama (Notaría Pública) / licensed Panamanian attorney acting as incorporator
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The registered agent or counsel drafts the Pacto Social y Estatutos together with the first board resolution. The subscribers execute the deed before a notary; alternatively, where a sole shareholder chooses the Executive Decree No. 153 de 2013 route, incorporation is executed as a private instrument with authenticated signatures. The instrument must contain the corporate name, domicile, authorized capital, share classes (if any), duration, board structure and appointment of the resident registered agent.
required_dossiers: Draft Articles of Incorporation (Pacto Social y Estatutos)
Certificado de Búsqueda of the corporate name
Passport or cédula copies of all subscribers
Registered agent appointment letter (Ley No. 5 de 2008)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Defects detected before filing are cured by executing a 'documento de rectificación' before the same notary and attaching it to the original instrument.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Inscription in the Public Registry and Issuance of Corporate Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá - Sección Mercantil (Vía José de Fábrega, Panama City)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Present the notarized deed (or private instrument) together with the registry fee for inscription. The Sección Mercantil assigns a corporate folio (ficha) and issues the certificate of inscription ('certificado de inscripción'), a certified copy of the charter, and the Certificado de Persona Jurídica. Express same-day service is available for an additional fee.
required_dossiers: Notarized deed or private incorporation instrument
Registry fee payment receipt
Certificado de Búsqueda of the corporate name
Identity documents of incorporators and officers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry issues a 'reparo' (query), counsel must present the corrected instrument and any clarifying schedule within thirty (30) days; an unfavorable decision may be challenged through a 'recurso de reconsideración' before the Dirección General of the Registry.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Adoption of Corporate Books and Initial Governance Records
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporate registered office / registered agent (no public filing required)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The company must maintain its statutory books at the registered office: Share Register (Libro de Registro de Acciones), Shareholders' Minutes Book and Board Minutes Book, each bound, foliated and sealed. Record the issuance of the subscribed shares, the adoption of the registered office, and the election of the President, Secretary and Treasurer from the first board resolution.
required_dossiers: Copy of the inscribed Articles of Incorporation and first board resolution
Share subscription details and subscriber identities
Officer acceptance letters
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Defective or unbound books are replaced and any omitted entry is restated by a supplementary board minute; regularization must occur before the following annual report filings.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registration with DGI and Issuance of RUC
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) - Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas; online 'Sistema T@x' portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After Registry inscription, apply on the DGI portal for the Registro Único de Contribuyente (RUC) using the certified corporate documents. Provide the legal representative's details, the registered-office address and the selected tax regime (territorial-source taxation). The DGI issues the RUC certificate, which is required for municipal licensing, banking, invoicing and employer registration.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of the inscribed incorporation deed
Certificado de Persona Jurídica issued by the Public Registry
Passport or cédula of the legal representative
Proof of registered office address
Completed RUC application form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: DGI 'observaciones' are cured by resubmitting corrected forms and supplementary evidence (such as a notarized power of attorney); if the account is temporarily blocked, request 'regularización de oficio' with the competent DGI desk.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Municipio de Panamá - Dirección General de Ingresos Municipales (online filing portal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the 'Solicitud de Aviso de Operación' for the S.A. at the municipality where the registered office or any physical service location operates. Attach the RUC certificate, corporate documents, address croquis and the fire-safety certificate if premises are occupied. Pay the municipal patent fee (based on authorized capital and economic activity) and receive the annual Aviso de Operación, which is the mandatory operating license for lawful invoicing in Panama.
required_dossiers: RUC certificate and certified corporate documents
Certificado de Persona Jurídica
Fire-safety inspection certificate (for occupied premises)
Address croquis and lease agreement
Completed municipal application and fee payment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Municipal queries or pre-inspection findings are corrected and re-filed within the municipality's stated term; tax-rate assessments may be appealed to the municipal revenue directorate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Caja de Seguro Social (CSS); Ministerio de Trabajo y Desarrollo Laboral (MITRADEL); Autoridad Nacional de Transparencia y Acceso a la Información (ANTAI)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Where the virtual CFO company hires Panamanian staff, register as an employer with the CSS (employer registration form) and file workplace personnel records with MITRADEL. Because the activity involves outsourced bookkeeping and payroll data, adopt client-data handling policies and, if personal data of data subjects in Panama is processed, make the required notification to ANTAI under Ley No. 81 de 2019.
required_dossiers: RUC certificate and certified corporate documents
Employer identification and address proof
CSS employer registration form and payroll data
MITRADEL personnel records
ANTAI data-processing notification (if applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Late registrations are regularized by filing the missing forms and paying administrative surcharges; ANTAI notifications, if deficient, may be rectified by filing an amended ex-ante notice.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Municipio de Panamá (Alcaldía de Panamá) - Dirección General de Ingresos Municipales, jointly with the Ministerio de Comercio e Industrias (MICI) - Registro de Empresas, which supervises the commercial and professional-services sector under ISIC 6920.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Aviso de Operación (Municipal Operating Notice/License for Commercial and Service Enterprises) - annual, mandatory for lawful invoicing in Panama; no separate industrial manufacturing permit applies to virtual CFO advisory services.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio de Ambiente (MiAMBIENTE) - Dirección de Evaluación de Impacto Ambiental
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category I (Low Impact) - simplified environmental registration/notice only; a full Environmental Impact Study (Categoría II/III) is not applicable to an office-based professional-services operation. MiAMBIENTE issues an environmental resolution or non-objection certificate upon filing; the municipal Aviso de Operación remains the controlling license for the physical office.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater, VOC or process-air emissions are generated by virtual CFO/BPO activity. Office sanitary wastewater discharged to the municipal sewer must comply with Resolución AG-0441-2007 (pH 6.0-9.0; BOD5 max 250 mg/L; TSS max 250 mg/L; oils and fats max 50 mg/L). E-waste and office solid waste are managed under Ley No. 41 de 1998 (Ley General del Ambiente) and the applicable municipal solid-waste bylaws.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire-safety inspection certificate from the Cuerpo de Bomberos de Panamá for the registered office; structural and occupancy load review by the Municipality; compliance with the occupational health and safety regulation (Decreto Ejecutivo No. 306 de 2004, MITRADEL); employer workplace records at the Ministerio de Trabajo y Desarrollo Laboral; and, where client personal data is processed, registration and compliance with Ley No. 81 de 2019 under the oversight of ANTAI.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas (MEF); official electronic taxpayer portal: 'Sede Electrónica' (https://dgi.mef.gob.pa), including RUC issuance, e-filing, and the Sistema de Facturación Electrónica de Panamá (SFEP) for fiscal invoice validation.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Panamanian Sociedad Anónima obtains its statutory tax ID through the following sequence: (1) file the incorporación deed with the Registro Público de Panamá and obtain the registered corporate existence certificate; (2) appoint a resident agent and legal representative as required by law; (3) apply online through the DGI Sede Electrónica for the RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyentes), attaching the public deed, identification documents of officers, and proof of registered address, using the digital eSignature granted by the DGI; (4) obtain the municipal patent and Aviso de Operación from the competent Alcaldía (Municipality); (5) for offshore service sellers, request DGI authorization to issue zero-rated ITBMS export invoices and register in the exporter services sub-ledger. Non-resident shareholding is unrestricted; Panama imposes no minimum capital for the S.A. and the RUC remains active even with zero Panamanian-source activity, subject to annual information filings.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Panama does not operate a US-style check-the-box regime. Elections statutorily available include: (i) the Small Taxpayer Simplified Regime (Régimen Simplificado) for taxpayers with annual gross turnover not exceeding B/. 300,000, offering consolidated quarterly compliance; (ii) the Multinational Company Headquarters regime (Sede de Empresa Multinacional, SEM, under Law 45 of 2012) for cross-border group service centers, potentially exempting certain foreign-source service income and ITBMS on intercompany services; (iii) advance pricing agreements (APAs) with DGI to stabilize intercompany margins for the fractional CFO services; (iv) preferential-zone elections (Panamá Pacífico, City of Knowledge) granting full income tax and ITBMS exemptions for qualifying service tenants; and (v) written advance rulings on territorial-source classification of export services. A standard S.A. with foreign clients and remote service delivery remains, absent election, within the territorial regime: only Panamanian-source income is taxed at the 25% corporate rate.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: ITBMS — Impuesto de Transferencia de Bienes Muebles y Servicios (Panamanian VAT)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: General rule: compulsory ITBMS registration from the first taxable transfer or service rendered in Panamanian territory; there is no general de-minimis exemption for a Panamanian S.A. issuing invoices. The B/. 300,000 (≈ USD 300,000) annual gross income threshold defines eligibility for the Simplified Small-Taxpayer Regime rather than exemption from registration. Non-resident digital service suppliers owe non-resident ITBMS registration under Law 192 of 2021 from their first Panamanian-source digital service revenue. A virtual-CFO consultancy holding a Panamanian RUC must be ITBMS-registered and file monthly returns irrespective of whether its revenue is entirely export-oriented.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Electronic invoicing is mandatory through the SFEP platform under DGI Resolution 201-4699 of 2019 and subsequent amendments. The S.A. must integrate its billing stack (including Stripe Billing and Wise payment records) with the DGI API over HTTPS: commercial invoices are transmitted in standardized XML format to the DGI before issuance for most registered taxpayers ('validación previa' real-time pre-clearance), the DGI returns a unique authorization number and a QR-coded fiscal seal (Sello Fiscal Electrónico) to be printed on the customer-facing PDF; smaller taxpayers may use 'validación posterior' batch upload through the Sede Electrónica. All e-invoices must be rendered in USD (Panamanian balboa is pegged 1:1), must identify the foreign client's tax ID for export invoices, and must be stored for the statutory six-year audit period; invoice voiding requires DGI-approved credit-note XML (NC) transactions.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports qualify at the 0% ITBMS rate where all of the following are satisfied: (i) the recipient is tax-resident or domiciled outside Panama and does not maintain a Panamanian permanent establishment benefiting from the service; (ii) the service is rendered to and 'used or exploited' entirely abroad — remote fractional CFO advisory, multicurrency bookkeeping and digitized management reporting delivered by the S.A. from Panama to foreign clients satisfy this territorial-export rule; (iii) the supplier is an ITBMS-registered taxpayer in good standing; and (iv) the supplier retains a complete substantiation file proving the foreign destination and payment. Input ITBMS on Panamanian overheads (bank charges, subscriptions, local legal and accounting services) is creditable against output ITBMS, and net credit balances arising from zero-rated exports are eligible for quarterly refund (devolución) from the DGI. Although Panama's dollarized economy imposes no statutory FX repatriation deadline, prudent practice requires documented receipt of the foreign currency consideration within 180 days of invoice issuance to survive DGI export verification.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Declaración de Exportación) — required where the service deliverable incorporates tangible media or goods moved outside Panama
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing physical exit of any exported goods; for pure remote services, a signed service delivery certificate and system/email logs evidencing offshore delivery
Inward Remittance Certificate issued by a Panamanian licensed bank or a foreign-currency receipt confirmation evidencing the US Dollar credit from the non-resident client
Zero-rated ITBMS e-invoice generated through SFEP, quoting the foreign client's tax identification number and a clear territorial-export rationale
Executed service agreement and statement of work defining the foreign place of supply, beneficial use outside Panama, and payment milestones
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DGI conducts targeted export-verification audits for service exporters claiming 0% ITBMS, with focus on false documentation, circular payments, and shell foreign recipients. Adverse findings trigger: (i) retrospective reclassification of the export as a taxable local supply — the entity must self-assess 7% ITBMS on the full invoice value plus statutory surcharges and moratory interest from the original filing date; (ii) monetary fines per the Código Fiscal up to 50% of the omitted tax and, for falsified records, fines of up to ten times the amount fraudulently refunded; (iii) criminal 'defraudación tributaria' liability — aggravated tax fraud may expose the officers and resident agent to imprisonment terms (up to 5 years under Panamanian tax criminal law) plus fines of up to three times the tax involved; and (iv) administrative clawback of refunds already paid with interest, suspension of the exporter registration, and revocation of the RUC's authorization to render zero-rated invoices for up to two fiscal years, effectively terminating the offshore services business model.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco Nacional de Panamá (fiscal agent) in coordination with the Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (SBP); Panama has no traditional central bank and operates under a fully dollarized monetary system with the US dollar as legal tender.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Panamanian balboa (PAB) is pegged at par to the US dollar, and the USD circulates freely alongside it. There are no exchange controls or restrictions on current-account or capital-account transactions. Non-resident shareholders may remit dividends, royalties, and liquidation proceeds abroad without prior central bank approval. Panama applies a territorial tax system; Panama-source income is taxed, but outbound profit remittances are generally free from withholding taxes when properly documented under domestic law.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Panama imposes no statutory surrender requirement, mandatory repatriation timeline, or conversion ratio on export proceeds. Exporters may retain funds in any currency and maintain USD-denominated bank accounts subject only to standard anti-money laundering (AML) reporting thresholds.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account / State-linked Settlement Account
Capital Escrow Account / High-net-worth Client Onboarding

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Moderate. Cross-border digital EMIs such as Wise and Stripe are viable for payment aggregation and disbursement but cannot provide regulated Panamanian clearing, deposit protection, or escrow-grade counterparty risk. A Panamanian commercial bank account remains mandatory for capital escrow, statutory liquidity, and high-value treasury operations; EMIs are accordingly treated as ancillary receivable collection rails rather than primary banking infrastructure.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Most Panamanian banks require at least one director or the ultimate beneficial owner to attend an in-person KYC interview before account opening. Limited remote video onboarding is occasionally permitted under SBP-guided enhanced due diligence where the beneficial owner has an existing banking relationship; however, fully remote opening for a wholly non-resident-owned Sociedad Anónima is uncommon and generally classified as higher compliance risk.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident, wholly foreign-owned S.A. with nominee directors and no local economic footprint
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified corporate registry excerpt (Registro Público) showing current officers and nominative shares, sworn director declarations, certified passports, proof of registered agent, and a detailed business plan explaining the virtual CFO services and expected clients.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Influx of initial capital from secondary-money-laundering-risk jurisdictions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bank reference letters from the sending institution, audited financial statements for the previous two fiscal years, source-of-wealth statement with third-party corroboration (tax returns, invoices, sale agreements), and completed beneficial ownership declaration.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Aggregated client funds passing through the corporate account for SaaS/CFO billing
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Segregated sub-account structure, transaction monitoring framework under SBP AML rules, underlying client KYC/onboarding records, and a written treasury policy demonstrating client fund isolation and reconciliation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Historical bearer-share legacy or outdated corporate registers
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Fresh registry excerpt confirming cancellation of bearer shares, current nominative share registry, notarized share transfer resolutions, and a copy of the latest Income Tax / annual return filing to validate standing.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: PEP connection or negative media mentions among beneficial owners
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Independent legal opinion on PEP status, enhanced adverse-media screening report, proper declaration of politically exposed persons, and a transparent chain of intermediaries with ongoing monitoring via SBP-compliant risk tools.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inward USD wires from foreign shareholders use SWIFT MT103 with purpose codes denoting equity contribution (e.g., 'Paid-up capital' or 'Capital injection'). Beneficiary accounts are held with a Panamanian commercial bank, and intermediate clearing flows through correspondent banks in New York (CHIPS/Fedwire) for same-day value. Verification at onboarding requires the board resolution authorizing the injection, a copy of the wire instruction, beneficial ownership declaration, and a letter of lawful origin of funds; amounts exceeding approximately USD 250,000 may trigger enhanced due diligence.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound settlements are executed by SWIFT MT103 for supplier payments, commercial letters of credit (LC) issued through the Panamanian bank with a confirming bank outside Panama, and bank guarantees for trade performance. USD clearing is completed via CHIPS/Fedwire or through Panama's local clearing house for checks; foreign-currency disbursements are handled via nostro accounts with correspondent banks.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Cross-Currency Swaps for long-term multicurrency liabilities

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Franchise Tax – Tasa Única Anual (corporate legal-existence renewal)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) of the Ministry of Economy and Finance, Panama (tax authority)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due on or before 31 January of each calendar year; the first year is prorated from the date of incorporation to 31 December and payable before the first 31 January deadline after incorporation.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment accrues statutory surcharges and default interest; the company loses good-standing status, cannot record documents in the Registro Público, and three consecutive unpaid years authorize the Public Registry to strike off or dissolve the S.A.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Income Tax Return – Declaración Jurada Anual del Impuesto sobre la Renta
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) – electronic filing portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For calendar-year taxpayers, due on or before 15 March of the following year; for fiscal periods other than calendar, within 3 months after fiscal year-end. A nil/exempt return is also required when no Panamanian-source income is derived.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or late filing triggers statutory fines and monthly default interest; the taxpayer's DGI clearance and good-standing certificates are withheld, and persistent non-filing may lead to estimated assessment by the DGI.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Register Audit and UBO Declaration Confirmation (to the resident agent)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registered Agent (repository of statutory books); no filing to Registro Público unless a transfer or directorship change has not previously been recorded
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: At the S.A.'s incorporation anniversary or within 15 days of the resident agent's annual compliance review; any share transfer must update the Register of Members and the UBO file immediately on transfer.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to maintain the Register of Members, Register of Directors, and Minute Book, or to refresh UBO information, is a corporate/AML violation carrying fines and loss of limited liability protection for certain bearer or unsettled transfers.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No general statutory audit requirement applies to a private Panama S.A. A mandatory independent audit is triggered when: the entity is a listed/issuer under the Superintendencia del Mercado de Valores (SMV); the entity holds a regulated financial, insurance, trust, gaming, or fund-administration license; the DGI expressly requires audited financial statements during a verification or transfer-pricing procedure; or a bank/financing agreement imposes an audit covenant. Unregulated service companies may conduct a voluntary audit at the directors' discretion.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as issued by the IASB is the recognized Panamanian accounting framework; private S.A. entities generally apply full IFRS or IFRS for SMEs, with statutory books maintained in Spanish and monetary records expressed in USD/Balboas.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Panama does not operate a public UBO registry. Under Law 52 of 2016 and AML rules, the licensed resident agent must know the beneficial owner of all shares and maintain an internal UBO file. The agent sends an annual UBO confirmation questionnaire to directors and shareholders; the signed confirmation is kept as a statutory record rather than filed with the government. Any transfer of shares requires an updated UBO disclosure before the company's Register of Members is amended. In practice, failure to provide the annual confirmation is treated as a UBO/AML compliance breach and may result in customer-due-diligence sanctions, fines, or limitations on the agent's ability to continue acting.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 450–1,200 for registered office and resident-agent service; USD 700–1,800 when annual secretariat, UBO/AML file maintenance, and statutory register audits are included
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,000–5,500 depending on transaction volume, multicurrency ledger complexity, and IFRS presentation depth

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% standard corporate income tax; 15% on the first USD 50,000 of net taxable income and 25% on the excess; qualifying micro-taxpayers may access a simplified gross-receipts regime of up to 2%.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Territorial taxation: only Panamanian-source income is taxable; foreign-source Virtual CFO service revenue may be excluded when performance and decision-making occur outside Panama; SEM / City of Knowledge incentives available for qualifying multinational service companies; deductions allowed for apportioned direct costs; NOL carryforward for 5 years.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulario 130 (Declaración Jurada de Renta de Personas Jurídicas) filed electronically via the DGI 'Sistema de Información Tributaria' (SIT) portal at www.dgi.gob.pa; Transfer Pricing annex cross-filed as Form 142.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; quarterly advance tax instalments and monthly ITBMS / withholding declarations are required during the year.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: On or before the last business day of the third calendar month following fiscal year-end; for calendar-year entities the deadline is 31 March of the following year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Ingresos Brutos: gross revenue in all currencies from all clients before deductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Segregate Panamanian-source revenue from foreign-source revenue; retain client contracts, performance evidence and ledger tags to support the split.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Rentas de Fuente Panameña: revenue sourced in Panama, including services rendered from Panamanian territory.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the foreign-owned S.A. renders CFO services remotely to foreign clients, document where decisions are made and where work is physically performed to mitigate Panamanian-source claims.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Rentas Exentas / No Sujetas: exempt income, including foreign-source income qualifying under the territorial regime.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Complete only with documentary support; the DGI will audit foreign-source claims for payroll, office and billing substance.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Costos y Gastos Deducibles: direct costs, subcontractor fees, software subscriptions, payroll and apportioned overhead.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply proportionate allocation between taxable and exempt revenue; a multicurrency ledger is mandatory for audit defense.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Renta Neta Gravable: taxable income after deductions and loss carryforwards.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident owners cannot offset personal foreign losses against the Panamanian S.A. net income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Impuesto Determinado: tax computed at 15% on the first USD 50,000 and 25% on the balance.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the DGI tariff schedule; no preferential dividend credit is taken at this line.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Créditos y Anticipos: quarterly advance CIT payments, withheld credits and eligible foreign tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign shareholder taxes are not creditable against Panamanian CIT; only DGI-issued credit vouchers are accepted.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Impuesto Neto a Pagar: final CIT liability after all credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Pay via the authorised Panamanian tax bank network; retain the ACH receipt for the company solvency certificate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Operaciones con Partes Relacionadas: related-party disclosure and Form 142 TP reference.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose shareholder loans, management fees, licensing of software and intercompany balances accurately.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: 5% surcharge on the tax due plus monthly interest of 1% per month or fraction; failure to file: administrative fine up to USD 5,000; inaccurate or fraudulent return: penalty of 25%-50% of the evaded tax; criminal tax evasion carries imprisonment of 2-5 years plus fines.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% general dividend withholding tax; reduced to 5% when the distributed profits have been fully subject to the 25% net corporate income tax; distributions of exempt or foreign-source profits may attract a 15.5% compensating dividend withholding where applicable.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Panama maintains a limited comprehensive DTA network. To invoke treaty relief, the non-resident beneficial owner must: (1) obtain a Certificate of Residencia Fiscal (TRC) from its residence jurisdiction; (2) submit the TRC, share registry extract and a treaty-benefit application to the DGI before the distribution date; (3) receive DGI approval to apply the reduced rate at source; and (4) if tax was over-withheld, file a refund claim within the three-year tax prescription period.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: 25% statutory withholding on gross Panamanian-source IP royalties, subject to treaty reduction. Interest: 6% withholding on interest paid to non-resident financial institutions for external financing; listed public-bond interest may be exempt; cross-border technical or administrative service fees may fall under the 12.5% service withholding characterisation.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Mandatory Form 142 Transfer Pricing information return where annual related-party transactions exceed USD 250,000; full Local File / Master File documentation maintained where Panamanian gross income exceeds USD 3,000,000 (Panama operates in USD).
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Panama does not impose a standalone Economic Substance Regulation filing comparable to BVI or Cayman; however, the DGI applies general anti-abuse and business-purpose doctrines, the SEM regime (Law 41 of 2007) imposes substance conditions for qualifying multinational headquarters, and the beneficial-ownership register under Law 23 of 2015 requires real presence indicators. A Virtual CFO S.A. must evidence local office, genuine employees, executed engagement contracts, local bank arrangements and decisions taken in Panama to defend its territorial-source position.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Criminal Tax Evasion and False Invoicing
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Consistently omitting Panamanian-source revenue from Form 130; under-invoicing foreign clients; fabricating deductions; maintaining undisclosed Stripe or Wise accounts that bypass the official ledger and SIT-FEL invoicing.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax surcharge of 25%-50% of the evaded amount plus 1% monthly interest; administrative fine up to USD 5,000; criminal fines up to 10 times the evaded tax and imprisonment of 2-5 years under Law 76 of 2019 reforms.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are jointly and severally liable for the evaded tax, surcharges and fines; precautionary attachment of personal assets, travel bans and disqualification from serving as directors of Panamanian companies.
